summary: The Goshen Township Zoning Commission held a public hearing on two final development plan cases. The first was Eagles Nest (ZC 2025-006), a 305-lot single-family residential portion of a larger 163-acre planned development mixed-use project on State Route 28 by the Drees Company, which was approved with seven stipulations. The second was Enclave Creek (ZC 2025-008), a 34-unit paired ranch-style condominium development on approximately 16 acres near Greenstone Trace and State Route 48, which drew significant public concerns about environmental damage, contractor conduct, stormwater management, and lack of developer representation at the hearing.
decisions: Approved Eagles Nest PDM final development plan (ZC 2025-006) with seven stipulations including open space requirements, connector roadway conditions, residential/commercial phasing enforcement, traffic impact study completion, streetscape standards, pedestrian connectivity with Kentucky four-board fencing allowing breaks for commercial signage, and Fay Road access in Phase 1
action_items: Future business/commercial/multifamily final development plans for Eagles Nest must provide at least 6.982 acres of qualifying net open space
Meadowcrest Circle street name to be changed to avoid confusion with existing Meadowcrest Lane
Kroger and Brandy Corp expected to submit commercial application for September/October meeting
Staff to enforce residential/commercial phasing at building permit stage using 555 residential unit threshold
Traffic impact study and associated State Route 28 road/intersection improvements to be completed
Bob Inkrot requested notification PDF be sent to him as he was missed in mailings across the street from Enclave Creek project
Residents advised to contact Clermont County Permit Central and county inspectors regarding contractor compliance issues at Enclave Creek

Victor Capitula (applicant for Enclave Creek, not present)
notes: The Enclave Creek developer (Victor Capitula) was notably absent from the hearing despite significant public opposition and an active stop work order on the property from Clermont County. Multiple residents expressed frustration about the developer's past conduct including unauthorized tree clearing, creek destruction, mud on streets, and construction quality issues. The transcript was truncated before the Enclave Creek vote was captured. A resident (Mark Orlando) raised concerns about inconsistent treatment between this Eagles Nest approval (5,000 sq ft lots, 10 ft between homes) and a previously denied Cozedale Road project that had larger lots and setbacks. Two commission members (Dinwiddie and Frisbee) were absent.
